newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China agrees to finance HK's government-in-waiting.
newsitem.headline: China agrees to finance HK's government-in-waiting.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader said on Sunday China would finance his government-in-waiting ahead of the colony's handover to Chinese rule on July 1.

"As for the funding question of the team-designate and the provisional legislature from mid-December to the end of June, the central government has expressed its support for the all financial expenditure," Tung Chee-hwa told reporters in Beijing following his first working level talks with Chinese officials.
The post-colonial Hong Kong government will provide its own funding after the handover when it starts collecting tax.
The former shipping magnate met Foreign Minister Qian Qichen and Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office director Lu Ping during his visit to Beijing.

Tung, chosen post-colonial leader on December 11 by a China-controlled 400-strong committee, said he had also raised the issue of the legal status of the provisional legislature with Chinese legislators.
"There are areas that the National People's Congress (NPC) needs to endorse which, I think, can be done," Tung said.
The NPC would study the legality of the interim assembly, due to hold its first meeting in China's southern city of Shenzhen by the end of January, he said.

Tung had said he may ask the NPC to pass a law endorsing the interim assembly, which will replace Hong Kong's current elected chamber. But he did not say whether he had made the request during the weekend visit.
Hong Kong will revert to China in 177 days time, ending more than a century and a half of colonial rule.

China, angered by Governor Chris Patten's democratic reform in the twilight of British rule, set up the interim chamber to reverse the reforms after the handover. Britain and Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement say the interim chamber violates a 1984 Sino-British agreement on the return of the territory.
Tung also gave fresh assurances to senior Hong Kong government officials that he would keep most of them in his administration according to their abilities.
Hong Kong's popular Chief Secretary, Anson Chan, had said she accepted Tung's invitation to remain in her post as the number two official in the territory's government.
The visit was 59-year-old Tung's second since his appointment as the Chief Executive. He was received by President Jiang Zemin, Premier Li Peng and Qian during his anointment on December 18.
